title: Lack of Control over Data Sharing
description: Parent user may not have adequate control over how their sensitive registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) is shared with the authentication service, potentially leading to unauthorized use or disclosure.
assumptions: User may not fully understand the implications of sharing sensitive personal information during registration.

title: Unintended Consequences of Data Sharing
description: Parent user may not be aware of the potential unintended consequences of sharing sensitive government ID and six-digit code information, which could lead to identity theft or fraud.
assumptions: User may not fully understand the risks associated with sharing government-issued identification and verification codes.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Sensitive registration data (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) transmitted from parent user to authentication service may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately encrypted or protected.

title: Lack of Control at Destination
description: Authentication service may not have adequate controls over how it stores, processes, and uses the received registration data, potentially leading to unauthorized access or misuse.
assumptions: Service may not implement proper access controls and data protection measures.

title: Data Deception at Destination
description: Authentication service may process or store the registration data in a way that deceives the parent user about how their information is used, stored, or shared.
assumptions: Service may not provide transparent data handling practices to users.

title: Unnecessary data collection for parent account storage
description: The authentication service may collect and store more parent account data than strictly required for authentication purposes, violating the minimality principle. This includes potentially storing unnecessary personal identifiers or metadata that could be used for profiling or linking.
assumptions: Assumes the system may collect more data than necessary for the stated purpose of storing parent account information.

title: Data disclosure through MongoDB storage
description: The MongoDB users collection may expose parent account data to unauthorized access or third-party disclosure. Data stored in the database could be accessed by malicious actors or leaked through database vulnerabilities, resulting in unintended disclosure of personal information.
assumptions: Assumes MongoDB database may have vulnerabilities or be accessible to unauthorized parties.

title: Data integrity risk in MongoDB storage
description: The stored parent account data may be tampered with, corrupted, or altered without detection. This could result in incorrect authentication data being used, potentially compromising user security and account integrity.
assumptions: Assumes the MongoDB storage may be subject to unauthorized modifications or data corruption.

title: Data linkability through flow metadata
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata that could be used to link or identify the parties involved. Information about the flow pattern, timing, or volume could potentially be used to infer relationships between users or their authentication activities.
assumptions: Assumes metadata about the data flow could be observed or analyzed by third parties.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of User Data
description: Authentication Service may disclose sensitive user data (including JWT tokens) to Parent User without proper authorization or consent, potentially violating user privacy expectations.
assumptions: Assumes Parent User is a legitimate recipient but may not have explicit consent for this data sharing.

title: Intrusion into Authentication Process
description: Authentication Service may be vulnerable to intrusion attacks that could compromise the integrity of JWT generation or user data handling before transmission.
assumptions: Assumes standard authentication service architecture with potential attack vectors.

title: Linkage via JWT Metadata
description: JWT tokens in transit may contain metadata (timestamps, user identifiers, session information) that could be used to link users across different authentication sessions or systems.
assumptions: Assumes JWT contains standard claims that may be observable during transmission.

title: Data Exposure During Transmission
description: JWT and user data transmitted over the network may be exposed to unauthorized parties through network sniffing, man-in-the-middle attacks, or insecure transmission channels.
assumptions: Assumes data may be transmitted over potentially insecure network paths.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure by Parent User
description: Parent User may disclose the received JWT and user data to unauthorized third parties, violating the privacy expectations of the original data subject.
assumptions: Assumes Parent User has control over the received data and may share it beyond intended recipients.

title: Intrusion into Parent User's Data Handling
description: Parent User may be vulnerable to intrusion attacks that could compromise the security of received authentication data, potentially leading to unauthorized access or data manipulation.
assumptions: Assumes Parent User system has potential security vulnerabilities.

title: Child User lacks control over data sharing
description: Child users may not have adequate control or understanding of what personal data (parent email, password) they are sharing during login, potentially leading to unintended data exposure.
assumptions: Assumes child users may lack full awareness of data implications

title: Data in transit may expose metadata
description: Login data in transit may contain metadata about parties being used to link or identify them, potentially allowing correlation attacks or tracking of child user authentication patterns.
assumptions: Assumes data flows over potentially insecure channels

title: Authentication service may be vulnerable to intrusion
description: Authentication service may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, allowing attackers to intercept, modify, or steal authentication credentials and user data.
assumptions: Assumes authentication service has access controls that may be bypassed

title: Authentication service may disclose sensitive data
description: Authentication service may inadvertently disclose sensitive authentication data or parent email information during processing or storage.
assumptions: Assumes authentication service has appropriate data protection measures

title: JWT can be used to link child user to other data
description: The JWT token contains user identifiers that could be used to link the child user to other authentication events, activities, or data sources, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across different systems.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted and stored in a way that preserves their identifiers

title: JWT and child profiles in transit could be intercepted
description: The JWT token and child profile data transmitted between Authentication Service and Child User could be intercepted by third parties during data transmission, potentially leading to unauthorized access or identity theft.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over a network that may not be fully secured

title: Child user could disclose JWT or child profiles
description: The child user receiving the JWT and child profiles could potentially disclose this information to unauthorized parties, leading to identity theft or unauthorized access to child data.
assumptions: Child user may not have adequate security practices or awareness

title: Parent provides identifying information for child
description: Parent user intentionally shares identifying data (name, DOB, govt ID) that enables identification of the child data subject. This is a legitimate identification act but creates privacy risk if the child is a minor.
assumptions: Parent is aware they are providing identifying information about a minor child.

title: Parent may link child profile to other data
description: Parent may be linking this child profile to other data they possess (medical records, school records, etc.) which could enable comprehensive profiling of the child.
assumptions: Parent has access to other data about the child and may combine it with this profile.

title: Flow metadata enables linking
description: Data in transit may contain metadata (timestamps, IP addresses, session information) that can be used to link this child profile to other data flows or identify the parent-child relationship.
assumptions: Network metadata is captured and analyzed by third parties.

title: Flow contains identifying information
description: The data flow itself contains identifying information about both the parent and child that could be intercepted and used for identification purposes.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without adequate encryption.

title: Child profile data may be disclosed
description: Child profile information (name, DOB, govt ID) stored in the system may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities or policy violations.
assumptions: System has appropriate access controls and security measures.

title: System may link child profile to other databases
description: The child profile management system may link this profile to other databases or systems, enabling comprehensive profiling of the child across multiple data sources.
assumptions: System has integration with other data repositories.

title: Potential non-compliance with minor data protection laws
description: Processing of child data may not comply with applicable data protection laws (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) requiring special consent and protection for minors.
assumptions: System has appropriate legal compliance measures for minor data.

title: Unauthorized data disclosure of child profiles
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized users or disclosed to third parties without proper access controls, violating privacy principles for sensitive minor data.

title: Data loss of child profiles
description: Child profile data could be lost due to system failures, corruption, or deletion without proper backup and recovery mechanisms, affecting data availability for legitimate purposes.

title: Over-collection of child profile data
description: The process may collect more child profile data than strictly required for profile management, violating the minimality principle for personal data of minors.

title: Excessive retention of child profile data
description: Child profile data may be retained longer than necessary, increasing privacy risk and compliance burden for sensitive minor data.

title: Data linkage through child profile metadata
description: The data flow itself could be used to link or identify individuals through metadata or derived information during storage operations.

title: Incomplete child profile data
description: Child profile data may be incomplete or inaccurate due to data entry errors or system limitations, affecting the quality of stored personal information.

title: Unavailability of child profile data
description: Child profile data may not be accessible when needed due to system failures, access restrictions, or technical issues, affecting legitimate data use.

title: Child user sharing excessive personal data for video search
description: Child user (EE2) may share more personal data than necessary for video search functionality, including age, location, and browsing history, which could be used for profiling or targeted advertising.
assumptions: Child users may not fully understand the extent of data they are sharing.

title: Child user identity linked to video preferences
description: Child user's identity may be linked to their video search patterns, likes, and comments, creating a profile that could be used for behavioral analysis or targeted advertising.
assumptions: Child users may not be aware that their interactions are being tracked and linked to their identity.

title: Child user data collection may violate COPPA/GDPR-K
description: Collection of personal data from children (under 13 in US, under 16 in EU) may violate COPPA (Children's Online Privacy Protection Act) or GDPR-K (GDPR for children) without proper parental consent mechanisms.
assumptions: The system may not have adequate parental consent mechanisms in place for child users.

title: Metadata in video search flow reveals user identity
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timestamps, IP addresses, device identifiers) could be used to link the child user to their video search activity, enabling tracking across sessions.
assumptions: Metadata is not properly anonymized or encrypted during transmission.

title: Video search data intercepted by third parties
description: Video search requests, likes, and comments transmitted over the network could be intercepted by malicious actors, leading to unauthorized access to child user's preferences and behavior.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over potentially insecure networks without proper encryption.

title: Video management service storing excessive personal data
description: Video Management Service (P2) may store more personal data than necessary for video search functionality, including location data, browsing history, and device information.
assumptions: Data retention policies may not be properly defined or enforced.

title: Video management service identifying users from search patterns
description: Video Management Service may identify users from their search patterns, likes, and comments, creating detailed profiles that could be used for behavioral analysis or targeted advertising.
assumptions: User identification mechanisms may not be properly anonymized.

title: Video management service non-compliance with child data protection laws
description: Video Management Service may not comply with child data protection laws (COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding data collection, storage, and processing of child user data.
assumptions: The service may lack proper compliance mechanisms for child data protection.

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata may contain identifying information (timestamps, location data, user identifiers) that can be used to link or identify individuals, even if not explicitly personal data.
assumptions: Metadata travels with video files during storage/retrieval operations

title: Data disclosure through storage
description: Storing video metadata and files in MongoDB collection may result in disclosure of personal data to unauthorized parties or through data breaches, violating minimality principle.
assumptions: MongoDB collection may be accessible to unauthorized parties or data may be exposed through security vulnerabilities

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: MongoDB collection storing child search and watch history may be accessible to unauthorized parties without proper access controls, violating the minimality principle for personal data storage

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: MongoDB collection storing child search and watch history may be vulnerable to unauthorized access by malicious actors or compromised system accounts

title: Data loss of child profile information
description: MongoDB collection storing child search and watch history may experience data loss or corruption due to system failures, accidental deletion, or storage errors

title: Metadata disclosure of child profile data
description: Data flow metadata could be used to link or identify children, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across different services

title: Unintended video data sharing
description: Parent user may inadvertently share sensitive or private video content without fully understanding the implications of the upload action.
assumptions: User may not be aware of the full scope of data being shared or the potential consequences.

title: User identity linked to video content
description: Parent user's identity may be associated with the uploaded video content, potentially revealing personal information about the user.
assumptions: Video upload process may include user identification or authentication mechanisms.

title: Video data integrity during transmission
description: Video data may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during transmission from Parent User to Video Management Service.
assumptions: Data may be transmitted over networks that could be vulnerable to interception or modification.

title: Unauthorized interception of video data
description: Video data in transit may be intercepted by unauthorized parties who could access or exploit the content.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or protected against interception.

title: Non-compliant video processing
description: Video Management Service may process video data in a manner that does not comply with applicable privacy regulations or data protection requirements.
assumptions: Service may lack proper privacy compliance mechanisms or may have inadequate data protection policies.

title: Unintended video content processing
description: Video Management Service may process video content without proper user consent or in ways that exceed the scope of the original upload request.
assumptions: Service may have broad data processing capabilities that could be used beyond the intended purpose.

title: Improper personal data management when sharing video with children
description: The Video Management Service may not properly manage personal data when sharing video content with child users, potentially violating child protection regulations and privacy laws.
assumptions: Assumes the service is responsible for data management compliance

title: Unintended consequences from video sharing
description: Sharing video content with children may have unintended privacy consequences, such as revealing sensitive information about the child or others, or enabling inappropriate use of the content.
assumptions: Assumes the service considers potential unintended consequences

title: Data integrity during video transmission
description: Video data in transit may be intercepted or modified, compromising data integrity and potentially exposing sensitive content.
assumptions: Assumes video transmission occurs over a network

title: Improper personal data management by child user
description: The child user may not properly manage the received video data, potentially violating privacy expectations or child protection regulations.
assumptions: Assumes the child user has some control over the received data

title: Child browsing data disclosure to AI engine
description: Transfer of child browsing data from DataStore to AI Recommendation Engine represents an explicit disclosure of personal data across a boundary. The minimality principle may not be satisfied if data collected exceeds what is strictly required for the AI recommendation purpose.
assumptions: Data transfer is intentional and by design as part of the system architecture.

title: Data interception during transit
description: Child browsing data in transit between DataStore and AI engine may be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive browsing behavior of children.
assumptions: Data flows over network infrastructure that may not be fully secured.

title: AI engine processing of child data
description: AI Recommendation Engine may process child browsing data in ways that exceed the original collection purpose, potentially creating derived profiles or using data for purposes beyond the intended recommendation function.
assumptions: AI engine has access to child browsing data and may process it for recommendation purposes.

title: Location of data processing
description: AI engine may process child browsing data in a location that does not comply with applicable privacy regulations, particularly given the sensitive nature of child data.
assumptions: AI engine location and jurisdiction are not fully defined or verified.

title: Explicit disclosure of browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine (P4) shares browsing data with third-party advertisers (EE3) as part of the planned data flow. This constitutes an explicit disclosure of personal data to an external party, which may violate the minimality principle if browsing data is not strictly required for the intended purpose.
assumptions: Browsing data contains personal information about user behavior and preferences

title: Data in transit may expose metadata about data parties
description: The data flow (DF14) from P4 to EE3 involves browsing data in transit. This data in transit may contain metadata that could be used to link or identify the parties involved, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across different systems.
assumptions: Data transmission protocols may expose metadata about the data being transferred

title: Third-party advertisers may process browsing data beyond intended scope
description: Upon receipt of browsing data, third-party advertisers (EE3) may process, store, or share this data in ways not intended by the original data subject, potentially leading to additional disclosures or unintended consequences.
assumptions: Advertisers may have their own data processing practices that extend beyond the original sharing intent

title: Potential information leakage through excessive data sharing
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may share more browsing data than strictly necessary with third-party advertisers, leading to information leakage beyond what is required for the intended purpose.
assumptions: Data sharing may include more personal data than minimally required

title: Unintended consequences from advertiser data usage
description: Third-party advertisers may use browsing data in ways not intended by the original data subject, such as targeted advertising, profiling, or sharing with other third parties, leading to unintended privacy consequences.
assumptions: Advertisers may have their own data usage policies that extend beyond the original sharing intent

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Government ID Images
description: The file system backend/uploads/ may be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive government ID images. This represents an implicit data disclosure where personal data is exposed through potential security vulnerabilities in the storage mechanism.

title: Excessive Data Sharing at Source
description: The Authentication Service may be sharing more government ID image data than strictly required for authentication purposes, violating the minimality principle in data collection and sharing.

title: Metadata Disclosure in Data Flow
description: Data in transit between Authentication Service and File System may contain metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them, potentially enabling profiling or identification of individuals.

title: JWT Disclosure at Source
description: Authentication Service shares JWT tokens that may contain sensitive user information, creating risk of disclosure if not properly protected during sharing.
assumptions: JWT contains user identity and session information

title: User Identification at Source
description: Authentication Service identifies users through JWT tokens, which may be used to track and identify users across sessions.
assumptions: JWT contains unique user identifiers

title: JWT Interception in Transit
description: JWT tokens in transit from Authentication Service to Browser localStorage may be intercepted by malicious actors or network vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Data flows over network without proper encryption

title: JWT Storage Disclosure
description: Browser localStorage stores JWT tokens that may be accessible to malicious scripts through XSS attacks, leading to unauthorized disclosure of user credentials.
assumptions: localStorage is vulnerable to XSS attacks

title: Unintended JWT Access
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage may be accessed unintentionally by other applications or scripts on the same domain, violating user privacy expectations.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to all scripts on same domain

title: Child History Data Linking Risk
description: Child history data transmitted in this flow may contain meta-data or recurring identifiers (timestamps, locations, activity patterns) that could be used to link this child to other data about the child or parent, potentially building unwanted profiles or revealing additional information about the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes child history data may include identifying attributes or patterns that could be correlated with other data sources.

title: Parent User Information Disclosure
description: Parent user (EE1) receives child history data which may contain sensitive information beyond what is necessary for parental review, potentially including information about other family members or the child's activities that could be misused or disclosed inappropriately.
assumptions: Assumes parent user may not have full understanding of what data is being received or how it will be used.

title: Unauthorized Data Sharing
description: Child Profile Management process (P3) may share child history data without proper authorization or consent from the parent, potentially violating privacy expectations or regulatory requirements.
assumptions: Assumes there may be gaps in authorization controls or consent management within the process.
